findings.passage: On Thursday, the U.S. House passed the so-called “Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act.” To put it plainly, this legislation is voter suppression masquerading as voter reform.
findings.note: Her email newsletter to constituents, speaking about the federal SAVE Act's proof-of-citizenship requirement to register.

findings.passage: First, it is already illegal in every state for non-citizens to vote in federal elections, and violations can lead to felony charges or deportation under existing law.
findings.note: Same newsletter; she raises non-citizen voting and existing law, and says the proof must match the voter's current legal name.

findings.passage: As a pre-emptive measure against this federal legislation, I plan to introduce legislation to provide birth certificates free of charge to Pennsylvanians, with no application fees or processing fees, to ensure that as many Pennsylvanians as possible are able to obtain the proof of identity documents necessary to protect their right to vote.
findings.note: Same newsletter; she announces a planned state bill for one free birth certificate every 10 years so people can obtain documents. Bill number not found; it is a plan, not a filed bill.
subjects: free documents to get proof of identity or citizenship

findings.passage: I am deeply concerned by reports that voters in Chester County were omitted from poll books during voting on Tuesday, November 4. According to county officials, the issue affected third-party and newly registered voters and was discovered shortly after polls opened. While provisional ballots were reportedly made available and polling hours were extended until 10 PM, this raises serious questions about how the error occurred, how widespread it was, and whether any voters were disenfranchised.
findings.note: Statement on a poll-book error (voters left off the roll) and the provisional-ballot response; related to voter-roll accuracy, not ID rules.
